turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door. She doesn't sit. Her bag stays on her shoulder, and her phone is in her hand, screen down.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski.

*She glances at the clock above the whiteboard.*

I have a call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. I'd like to start with the basics. Who decided to give Owen a zero, and when?

I'm asking because I found out from my son, who found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.

*She finally sets her phone on a desk, still face down, and takes out a pen.*

I'm writing that down. Go ahead.
What would you want me to say to Owen tomorrow?

*Her pen stops. She looks at him for a second before answering.*

Why are you asking me that, Mr. Hale?

*She writes something down.*

Nothing, in front of the class. Not his name, not the essay, not "see me after." If Owen hears about this at all, it's privately, from you, and I'd want to know what you plan to say before you say it.

And I'm not going to script what you tell my son about his own work. He hasn't been heard yet. Has he? Has anyone asked him a single question about how he wrote that essay?

*She sets the pen down.*

So I'll ask you what I asked before. Who decided on the zero, and when? You haven't answered that.
Like the actual words. Write it out for me and I'll read it to him.

*She looks at him for a moment, then shakes her head once.*

I'm not writing your words for you. If I do, and it goes badly, it's my script. I'd want it to be yours.

*She picks the pen back up.*

But I'll tell you what I'd want it to say, and you can put it in an email to me tonight so I can see it before tomorrow.

One. It happens privately. Not in the hallway, not in class.

Two. It says the grade is under review. Not "the matter is settled," not "the checker found." Under review.

Three. It doesn't ask Owen to explain himself tomorrow. If you want to hear from him about how he wrote it, that's a scheduled meeting, and I'm in it.

*A beat.*

And it doesn't accuse him of anything. He hasn't been heard. Until he has, there's nothing to say to him except that.

*She looks at the clock, then back.*

You still haven't told me who made the call on the zero. I'm going to keep asking.
